questions.q: Superuser/sysadmin elevation is detected on an account not in the designated DBA principal list. Which reconciliation tier does this hit?
options: Auto-remediate, like a stale service-account grant
Stage for review via a GitOps pull request
Alert immediately — page on-call regardless of time
Log for the quarterly access review
questions.explain: The three tiers are auto-remediate (low blast radius), stage-for-review (new grants), and alert-immediately for sysadmin elevation — confidence for automated action scales inversely with blast radius.

questions.q: In the JIT privilege system, what enforces grant expiry?
options: The jit.usp_enforce_expiry procedure, run on a schedule every minute, revoking grants past expires_at
Manual DBA revocation each morning
The approval API's built-in timer
The drift-reconciliation loop every 4 hours
questions.explain: The expiry enforcer polls jit.active_grants for unrevoked grants past expires_at and issues the REVOKE, so privilege hygiene is structurally guaranteed rather than dependent on human memory.

questions.q: What prevents the automated data classifier from overwriting a classification a security officer set manually?
options: Classifications expire nightly
Only DBA principals may run the scanner
The MERGE upsert includes a human-review guard (WHERE reviewed_by = 'auto_classifier'), so manually set classifications are never overwritten
Manual overrides are stored in a different database
questions.explain: The persist_classifications method only updates rows whose reviewed_by is 'auto_classifier', respecting a human's decision to mark a column PUBLIC even if it looks sensitive.

questions.q: A non-DBA session executes sp_addsrvrolemember granting sysadmin. How does the escalation detector respond?
options: Logs it for the weekly review queue
Classifies it CRITICAL, terminates the principal's sessions, disables the login, and alerts
Retries the statement to confirm intent
Adds the source IP to the allowlist
questions.explain: Hard escalation fingerprints (SYSADMIN_ADD, CONTROL_GRANT) bypass the behavioral baseline entirely: CRITICAL triggers session termination plus login disable, HIGH terminates sessions, MODERATE alerts only.

questions.q: How does the chapter's dynamic RLS design propagate runtime claims (tenant ID, clearance level) into policy evaluation?
options: Via SQL Server Audit policies
Through Windows group membership
Via hard-coded application-name lists in the predicate
Via SESSION_CONTEXT() set by the connection wrapper with sp_set_session_context and read by the security predicate function
questions.explain: The predicate function reads app_tenant_id and app_clearance_level from SESSION_CONTEXT, making RLS a dynamic control surface that adapts to runtime context.
